name: Precision Engineering
summary: The discipline of machining and measuring to tight tolerances, enabling interchangeable parts and modern manufacturing, descended directly from lathe technology.

claims.statement: Wilkinson's precision boring machine (1774) enabled Watt's steam engine by achieving cylinder tolerances previously impossible
Maudslay's screw-cutting lathe established the foundation for standardized measurement and interchangeable parts
Japanese precision manufacturing achieved sub-micron tolerances by the 1970s, representing independent refinement of Western origins

evidence.source: Rolt (1965) Tools for the Job: A History of Machine Tools to 1950, Batsford
Maudslay's original screw-cutting lathe, Science Museum London, inventory 1900-56
Musson & Robinson (1969) Science and Technology in the Industrial Revolution, Manchester UP
JIS B 0401 (Japanese Industrial Standards for tolerances and fits)

notes: Borderline keystone: longevity below 300-year threshold, low decentralization (capital-intensive). Strong replication and lineage. Demonstrates how a technology can score differently depending on criteria weighting — a useful test case for the proof system.
